# Open-weights Model

An open-weights model is a [Large Language Model (LLM)](/resources/llm-knowledge-base/large-language-model-llm "LLM Knowledge Base: Large Language Model (LLM)") whose parameters (or "weights") are publicly accessible and can be used and modified without restriction.

Unlike closed or [Proprietary Models](/resources/llm-knowledge-base/proprietary-model "LLM Knowledge Base: Proprietary Model"), open-weights models are often shared within the AI community for research, educational purposes, or to foster innovation. They can be [fine-tuned](/resources/llm-knowledge-base/fine-tuning "LLM Knowledge Base: Fine-tuning") or adapted to specific tasks and contribute to the transparency and collaborative advancement of AI technology. Open-weights models can also facilitate reproducibility in AI research, allowing others to validate and build upon existing work.

Open weights also allow independent deployment optimizations such as [quantization](/resources/llm-knowledge-base/quantization "LLM Knowledge Base: Quantization"), which can reduce memory requirements for local or lower-cost inference.

In contrast to [Open-source Models](/resources/llm-knowledge-base/open-source-model "LLM Knowledge Base: Open-source Model"), open-weights models do not provide access to the model architecture or source code for the training pipeline.

In an [interview with Sequoia Capital](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=c3b-JASoPi0), [Andrej Karpathy](https://x.com/karpathy "Andrej Karpathy on X") used a nice analogy to software, saying "an open-weights model is a little bit like tossing over a binary for an operating system."

Examples of open-weights models are the [LLaMA series](https://developer.meta.com/ai/ "Meta LLaMA models") by [Meta AI](https://ai.meta.com "Meta AI website") and [Mistral 7B](https://mistral.ai/news/announcing-mistral-7b/ "Mistral 7B announcement post") / [Mixtral 8x7B](https://mistral.ai/news/mixtral-of-experts/ "Mixtral 8x7B info") by [Mistral AI](https://mistral.ai "Mistral AI announcement post").

The [LLM Knowledge Base](/resources/llm-knowledge-base "Bite-sized explanations for common terms related to Large Language Models") is a collection of bite-sized explanations for commonly used terms and abbreviations related to Large Language Models and Generative AI.

It's an educational resource that helps you stay up-to-date with the latest developments in AI research and its applications.
